name: Curiosity Gap
description: Opens on a question the episode answers and refuses to answer it in the description. A one-line hook, three withheld promises, then a short orientation paragraph, then the ask. Built for a browse-page click rather than a subscriber who already trusts the channel.
architecture: A withheld question up front, three teasers, orientation, then the ask.

sections.instruction: Write a single sentence posing the central question this episode answers. It must be a real question the episode genuinely resolves. Do not answer it and do not hint at the answer.

Write exactly three lines, each beginning with an arrow character and a space. Each line names something the episode reveals without revealing it. Each line is a fragment, not a full sentence, and under twelve words.

One short paragraph saying plainly what the episode covers and roughly how it is structured, so a viewer knows what they are committing to. This is the only place where a straight answer is allowed, and even here it stays at the level of subject rather than conclusion.
One sentence inviting the viewer to comment with their own guess at the answer before they watch. Then a second sentence asking them to subscribe. Keep both short and unforced.
Emit only hashtags, on a single line, separated by spaces. No sentence, no heading, no commentary.

title_plan.guidance: Front-load the unanswered question. Short, specific and concrete. Never promise a result the episode does not deliver, and never use the words shocking, insane, or you won't believe.

tag_plan.guidance: for this question-led explainer episode, weighted toward the phrases somebody would type when they already want this answer

constraints: Never state the episode's conclusion in the description.
No clickbait superlatives: nothing is shocking, insane, or unbelievable.
Every promise made here must be one the episode actually keeps.
